To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) pleural infection is a serious disease, with a high mortality rate; (2) early diagnosis, appropriate antibiotics and prompt drainage of the infected pleural cavity are the cornerstones of treatment; and (3) recent advances in the imaging, drainage and adjunctive therapy of pleural septic disease have improved the outcome of patients with pleural infection.

the use of flexible, image‐guided, catheter‐directed drainage is superior to tube thoracostomy, and that adjunctive intrapulmonary urokinase therapy reduces the length of hospital stay in patients with empyema.

(1) the use of flexible, image‐guided drainage tubes, in conjunction with antibiotics, is associated with a lower mortality than the use of intercostal tubes; (2) the use of intrapleural fibrinolytics, in conjunction with flexible drainage, is associated with an improved outcome in the management of empyema; (3) interventional thoracoscopic debridement is an effective and safe alternative to open surgery for the management of complicated empyema.
